title: Departures: where does our 84-field discrete diffusion code depart from MD4 and LLaDA?
headline: Seven of 15 parts follow MD4 or LLaDA; the other eight are ours alone
setup: Our model writes a team of six Pokémon as 84 fields. We split its code into 15 parts, such as how fields are hidden in training and in what order they are filled. Each part was compared with two published papers, MD4 and LLaDA. A second check then verified all 45 cells: 15 parts for ours and for each paper.
alt: Seven of the 15 parts match MD4 or LLaDA: five match MD4, three match LLaDA, and one matches both. The other eight are ours alone. Two of those, the masking rate and the decoding order, are tested by the four new rows. A third, the t told while sampling, was tested and had no effect.
terms: One design choice in our code, such as the masking rate or the decoding order. There are 15
Our code does the same thing as that paper in this part
No paper does it our way: the paper differs, or has no such part
A number from 0 to 1 that the model is told: how much of the team is still hidden
The order the sampler fills fields in. Ours: all six species first. The papers: random, or most confident first
The four ways of training and sampling that this map will battle, to test the masking rate and the decoding order

frames.title: 3. What the second check changed

items.text: Stat Points as tokens, MD4: now the same. Pixel values are 256 tokens
Validation draws, MD4: now differs. 32 draws on one benchmark
Validation draws, LLaDA: 128 draws, or 1 for one-token answers
Guidance mixing, LLaDA: same form, used only in an appendix test
Legal filter while sampling, ours: every value reopens if none is legal

frames.takes: A second check changed five of 45 cells, and the matching count rose from 6 to 7 of 15.
frames.measured: Each correction was confirmed at its quoted line in the paper's LaTeX source.

frames.title: 4. The three departures this map tests

Decoding order: species first against random, tested by the four new rows
t told while sampling: tested, no effect

frames.takes: Masking rate and decoding order are not run yet; the four rows written before any result test them.
frames.expected: Linear, random order loses to Linear, species-first, with an error under 2.8 times as large.
frames.surprise: A linear row that wins by 0.002 or more.
